attributes.[data-revealed]: the element a link or result led to, until the next

attributes.table.grid[data-lens] and td.cell[data-l: the statuses switched on in the legend, and their cells

creates.css_highlight: ::highlight(qh-find) over the search words in the element a result led to (no DOM change)

styles_required: No style is injected by status.js. The interaction states above are styled only by the CSS block in proposals/ (append status-css-block.css to status.css and status-print-css-block.css to status-print.css); without it they are functional but plain.

address.params: q, in, status, show are written by status.js; values the page does not have are named in a notice and dropped on arrival; every other parameter is kept
address.hash: an element id; unknown, malformed or hidden targets -> cancelable qh:unknown-anchor, then a notice with a search for the address's words; #find-q and #find-results open the search
address.push: search result, in-page link (native), tally link (?status=, no hash), qh:navigate, Continue reading, a row opened from a non-row address; the tally link adds in=<the page's parts> only when a component offers search units
address.replace: typing, chips, Show filter, opening a row from a row address or none, closing the row the address names
address.history_state: history.state.qh = {open: [disclosure keys], back: {id} | {hit, limit} | {within, n}}; written before leaving an entry and on every toggle; read on Back, Forward and reload; other keys and foreign states are kept. An entry with no back record (Forward, a link the browser follows, a typed address) puts focus on the element its hash names.
address.disclosure_key: its id, else 'in:' + the first id inside it, else '<nearest id>:<class>'

storage.localStorage qh-place: {id, title, at}: the part at the top of the screen when scrolling stops; offered once on a later plain visit, only while its address still names a part with that title; Close forgets it
storage.rule: every access in try/catch; nothing depends on storage

atlas.isolation: events starting inside [data-atlas-mount] are ignored by every page listener; page lookups exclude the mount; shared: the glossary card of .term[data-term]

atlas_to_page.qh:navigate: dispatch from inside the mount, bubbles, cancelable, detail {id}: the page reveals #id (an id of the page, not of the atlas), pushes an entry, focuses it and records the dispatching element for focus return; it calls preventDefault when handled
atlas_to_page.qh:content-changed: dispatch on document after adding or replacing page content: the page finds mounts again and rebuilds the search units
atlas_to_page.data-qh-unit: an element with an id and data-qh-unit (title: its [data-qh-unit-title]) is a search unit under the atlas part; optional data-qh-unit-status (one of the page's status values, as data-status writes them: its words and mark come from the status key, and the Status chips include the unit) and data-qh-unit-place (words naming where it sits, shown as the result's place and searched as such)

page_to_atlas.qh:state: on document after search, filter and address changes: detail {q, scopes, statuses, show, hash}
page_to_atlas.qh:reveal: on an offered unit when a search result leads to it, bubbles, cancelable, detail {id}: the atlas shows and focuses it and calls preventDefault; otherwise the page scrolls to it and focuses it
page_to_atlas.qh:unknown-anchor: on document, cancelable, detail {id}: a component that owns the address calls preventDefault and the page shows no notice

atlas.atlas_must_not: write the page's address or history itself, or use the page's hook classes (foundation ATLAS_RESERVED_CLASSES)
atlas.observed: the atlas lane's atlas.js does not cancel qh:reveal, so the page's fallback (scroll and focus) runs; cancelling is the atlas's choice; '/' does not open the page's search while focus is inside the mount (the atlas may forward it)
atlas.tally: a tally link lists the page's own statements: when a component offers units, the link limits the search to the page's parts (in=…), so its list count equals the tally's count
atlas.atlas_links: a link inside the mount is never handled by the page, but the search typed before it is written into the entry it leaves

served_hooks.[data-find]: optional served search mount (proposals/STATUS-PY.md P6 serves it after the tally, hidden until the script runs); its data-label-<name> attributes replace the interface words, from page.json "interface"
served_hooks.[data-needs-script][hidden]: served hidden, shown by status.js (proposals/STATUS-PY.md P2)
served_hooks.[data-find-open]: a control that opens the search

label_notes.more: Show {k} more ({k}: how many it adds, {n}: the total)
label_notes.hint: no longer promises "from anywhere": the atlas keeps its own keys

proposals_for_foundation.summary: proposals/STATUS-PY.md (P1 served statement ids, P2 script-only controls served hidden, P3 served descriptions, P4 TeX-free mark names) and the CSS block; exact patches and hashes there
proposals_for_foundation.P3 (revised): a mark is described by its scope paragraph only (the id moves from .cell-note to its scope p)
proposals_for_foundation.P6: serve <div data-find data-needs-script hidden data-label-…> after the tally, with words from page.json "interface"
proposals_for_foundation.P2b (proposal only): split the grid hint: hide "Select a mark for its scope." without the script, keep "On a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways." (page.json grid_hint split by its owner)
proposals_for_foundation.P5 (proposal only, open): terms and marks served as links (a.term[href=#term-…], marks to their row line) so no control is inert without the script; status.js already accepts any element type for .term and .cell-btn
proposals_for_foundation.content ids (content owner): every statement should carry a content id; statements without one are addressed by their title words and change address when the title does

status_values.rule: status.js holds no status vocabulary: every status is the served data-status of a statement or cell and the data-filter of a Show filter chip or tally link, compared as an opaque string; a value may have spaces ('refuted form', written st-refuted-form, chip-refuted-form, mark-refuted-form in class names) and is written into the address as status=refuted+form or show=refuted+form
status_values.refuted form for statements (content-con: works without a change to status.js: reader-task test 'a statement status of two words (refuted form) works in the filter, the address, the tally, the search and the legend' (synthetic card, on the baseline and the foundation producers)
status_values.needs from the foundation: serve, for every status that statements carry, its Show filter chip, its tally entry, its status-key item (the search names a status by the key's words) and its chip label; never coerce 'refuted form' to 'open'
status_values.needs from the atlas: data-qh-unit-status carries the page's value ('refuted form'), not the atlas's own name ('scoped_negative'); otherwise the unit shows no status and the Status chips leave it out
